Forbidden.description: Wrong Host (unknown_host), an Origin header (origin_refused), a scope the device lacks (forbidden_scope; see each operation's x-ainkrad-scope), or an operation marked x-ainkrad-destructive without a live step-up elevation (step_up_required)

Unauthorized.description: auth_failed (any signature or device failure, alike whatever the reason), clock_skew (with server_time), or session_expired

description.description: What the admin wrote about it.

paused_at.description: When the admin paused it; absent unless it is paused by the admin.

ApiVersion.description: The contract a server speaks: `/api/<major>` and its additions so far.

Appearance.description: How the client draws an agent's figure (decision #61).

sas.description: The SAS shown on both screens.

scopes.description: Narrower scopes than the pairing bound; never wider.

entity_id.description: A numeric entity id; absent for a device, which is named by `entity_ref` only.

entity_ref.description: The entity's public id: a device's opaque `d_…` id, else `entity_id` as text.

AuditPage.description:
A page of the audit log, newest first. `next_before` continues with older rows, absent on
the last page.

challenge.description:
32 bytes, base64url (43 characters), opaque to the client; spend it once within
`expires_in` seconds.

options.description:
A passkey device's step-up only: `{"publicKey": PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions}`
over `challenge`, for `navigator.credentials.get`.

device_id.description: The device that will answer it, `d_…`.

ClaimBody.description:
A claim. The credential hash is SHA-256 of the canonical typed code (upper-cased, dashes
and spaces dropped, `I`/`L` read as `1` and `O` as `0`: 10 ASCII Crockford characters), or
of the QR secret's 16 decoded bytes (not its base64 text). Vectors:
`crates/server/tests/vectors/pairing-v1.json`.

code.description: The typed code (`ABCDE-FGHJK`, any case); or `secret`.

pop.description:
The routine key's ES256 signature (raw r||s, base64url) over the UTF-8 string
`AINKRAD-PAIR-V1` LF `<core_fp>` LF `<base64url of the credential hash>` LF
`<fp(routine)>` LF `<fp(stepup) or ->`, no trailing newline; fp is base64url SHA-256 of
the SPKI.

pop_stepup.description: The step-up key over the same string, with `stepup_spki`.

routine_spki.description: The routine key: a P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64url.

stepup_spki.description: The step-up key, where the device has one.

core_spki.description: The Core identity SPKI, base64url: its fingerprint must equal the QR's `c`.

device_id.description: The new device, `d_…`, pending until approved.

pairing_id.description:
The pairing, `p_…`: with `core_spki` and its own key the device computes the SAS
itself and shows that, rather than trusting `sas` from whoever answered.

sas.description:
Show this; the approver compares it with theirs. The first 16 upper-case Crockford
characters of SHA-256(`AINKRAD-SAS-V1` ‖ core_spki ‖ routine_spki ‖ pairing id as
UTF-8), as `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`.

account_ids.description: The pool accounts its runs may use (E15.1); empty until the accounts slice.

color.description: Its colour, `#rrggbb`; absent when unset, as every optional field here.

description.description: What it does, for its agents (empty when unset).

logo_url.description: Its uploaded logo (`getCompanyLogo`); absent when it has none.

work_days.description: Working days as a bitmask: bit 0 Monday ... bit 6 Sunday (31 = Monday to Friday).

anyOf.description: The admin's own company, or a client's (E15.14).

Deleted.description: The answer to a delete: the id that is gone.

head_agent_id.description: The agent that heads it; absent when it has none.

Device.description: A device: who it is and what it may do. Never a key's private half: the Core has none.

fingerprint.description: base64url SHA-256 of its routine public key: what pairing shows.

key_storage.description: Where its key lives, as the device claims it (not verified).

last_used_at.description: Marked at most once a minute.

scopes.description: What it may do (E1-09 enforces them).

stepup.description: Whether it enrolled a step-up key, so it can elevate (E1-09.3).

anyOf.description: How hard an agent thinks (API minor 17).

elevated_until.description: Until when this session may call routes marked `x-ainkrad-destructive`.

ErrorBody.description: A JSON error: a stable `code` and a message for people.

error_id.description:
`err_` and a ULID, unique to this answer: logged with it (and, for a refused write,
audited as `api.refused`), for the app's "Copy error".

server_time.description: The server's clock in unix seconds, on a `clock_skew` refusal only (handshake spec §5.3).

Event.description:
One entry of the event stream. `seq` only grows: it is the replay cursor, counted gap-free over
the events this device's scopes may see (`x-event-scopes`), so it differs between devices
with different scopes. New kinds may be added: a client skips an event whose kind it does not
know.

kind.description:
What happened: `audit` (an audited change; the payload is the audit row: `audit_seq`,
`action`, `actor_kind`, `actor_id`, `entity_kind`, `entity_id`, `entity_ref`, `details`;
a device is named by its `d_…` id in `entity_ref`, with `entity_id` null), or a kind a
module writes. The registered kinds are listed in `x-event-kinds`.

EventActor.description: Who acted, on an audited change.

Handshake.description: What the server is and speaks, for anyone.

api_minor.description: The contract minor this server speaks (`GET /api/v1/me` has it too).

git_sha.description: The commit it was built from (short sha), when the build knew it.

identity_fingerprint.description:
`core_fp`: base64url SHA-256 of the Core identity key's SPKI, 43 characters. Signed
into every request (handshake spec §5.2).

supported_minors.description:
Every minor a client may have been built against and still be served: 0 up to
`api_minor`.

HandshakeBody.description: A liveness proof request: a fresh nonce from the client.

nonce.description: 16 random bytes, base64url without padding (22 characters).

HandshakeProof.description:
`POST /handshake`'s answer: `GET`'s fields plus the proof, which is always present (review
L4). A client that pinned `core_fp` aborts with `core_identity_mismatch` when either is
missing or fails, and never falls back to `GET /handshake` (spec §13).

core_sig.description:
The Core identity key's ES256 signature (raw r||s, base64url) over the UTF-8 string
`AINKRAD-CORE-V1` LF `<host>` LF `<nonce>`, no trailing newline; `host` is the Core's
configured Host (the `Host` it requires), `nonce` the text the client sent.

core_spki.description:
The Core identity key, a P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64url. Its fingerprint is
`identity_fingerprint`.

identity_fingerprint.description: `core_fp`, as in `GET /handshake`; a client checks `fp(core_spki)`, not this claim.

LatestEvent.description: The newest event's seq a client would be shown: the catch-up target.

floor.description:
The retention floor: events up to it were trimmed, so a client whose last read seq is
below it re-syncs (E1-04.4). Absent from servers before API minor 2.

Lockout.description: A key that is locked now.

strikes.description: Locks in a row; each doubles the next.

Me.description: The calling device and what the server speaks.

Named.description: A device: who, by id and name.

kind.description: `own` (the default) or `client`; anything else is a 400.
`device`, `runner`, or `passkey` (a browser, E1-08; only when the Core has passkeys).

name.description: What to call the new device.

scopes.description: What it may do: within the approver's own scopes; a runner gets exactly `runner`.

Page_Event.description: A page of a list. `next_after` is the cursor of the next page, absent on the last.

code.description: The typed code, `ABCDE-FGHJK`: shown once, good once, for 5 minutes.

qr.description: `ainkrad-pair:v1?h=…&p=…&c=<core_fp>&s=<secret>&e=…`, for a QR code: shown once.

PairingView.description: A pairing as the approver sees it.

key_storage.description: Where the claimant says its key lives: a claim, not verified.

sas.description:
The SAS the Core computed from its key and the claimant's: compare it with the new
device's screen, then send it back to approve.

code.description: The same code as for the options; or `secret`.

credential.description:
The created credential as a WebAuthn `RegisterPublicKeyCredential` (`id`, `rawId`,
`type`, `response.attestationObject`, `response.clientDataJSON`, optional
`response.transports`), binary fields base64url.

code.description: The typed code (`ABCDE-FGHJK`, any case); or `secret`.

expires_at.description: The pairing's expiry: the credential must be claimed before it.

options.description:
`{"publicKey": PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions}` (WebAuthn, binary fields base64url):
ES256 only, attestation `none`, user verification required, a resident key preferred.
Decode it and pass it to `navigator.credentials.create`.

PastRetention.description: The 410 of a replay from below the retention floor (E1-04.4).

floor.description: The newest trimmed seq: every event above it is still there.

sandbox.description: A development build's token, for the sandbox gateway.

token.description: The device token, hex, as the app got it from APNs.

name.description: 1 to 64 characters, no control characters; trimmed.

Runner.description: A paired runner and its live state.

degraded.description: Connected but silent past two heartbeats.

drivers.description: What it last advertised (empty until it first connected since the Core started).

last_seen.description: Its last frame or request; null if never seen.

RunnerDriver.description: A driver a runner offers, as it advertised it.

capacity.description: How many of its commands run at once.

anyOf.description:
What an agent's harness may touch (API minor 17): `read-only`, `workspace-write` or
`full-access`.

elevated_until.description: Until when the session is elevated (E1-09); null when it is not.

session_id.description: `s_…`: sent as `Ainkrad-Session` on every signed request. Not a secret.

challenge.description: A live challenge issued for the signing device.

scopes.description: From the catalogue, each held by the calling device; a runner holds exactly `runner`.

SetSetting.description: A value to set: an integer in the setting's unit.

Setting.description: One setting and its effective value at the scope asked about.

min.description: The bounds a value must be within.

scopes.description: Where it may be set; the most specific with a value wins.

source.description: Where `value` was set (`server`); absent: the default.

SettingChange.description: One set or reset, newest first.

new.description: What was set; absent for a reset.

old.description: What was set at `scope` before; absent when it inherited.

assertion.description:
A passkey device's proof: the WebAuthn `PublicKeyCredential` answering the challenge's
`options`, with user verification.

challenge.description: The challenge from `POST /api/v1/auth/step-up/challenge` for this session.

stepup_sig.description:
The step-up key's ES256 signature (raw r||s, base64url) over the UTF-8 string
`AINKRAD-STEPUP-V1` LF `<core_fp>` LF `<device_id>` LF `<session_id>` LF `<challenge>`,
no trailing newline. The device's OS releases that key only after user verification.
Required for a native device; a passkey device sends `assertion` instead.

Timestamp.description:
RFC 3339 UTC with exactly milliseconds, `2026-10-21T12:00:00.250Z`: one shape, so a
client's date parser never meets a second one (E0.4).

Versions.description: What the server is and speaks.

git_sha.description: The commit it was built from (short sha), when the build knew it.

options.description:
`{"publicKey": PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions}` (WebAuthn, binary fields base64url),
user verification required, no credential list (the passkey is discoverable): decode
it and pass it to `navigator.credentials.get`.

session_spki.description:
The browser's session key: a non-extractable WebCrypto ECDSA P-256 key's SPKI
(`exportKey("spki")` of its public half), base64url.

session_id.description: `s_…`: sent as `Ainkrad-Session`; every request is signed with the session key.

credential.description:
The assertion as a WebAuthn `PublicKeyCredential` (`id`, `rawId`, `type`,
`response.authenticatorData`, `response.clientDataJSON`, `response.signature`,
`response.userHandle`), binary fields base64url.

ticket.description:
16 random bytes, base64url: offer `ainkrad.v1, ainkrad-ticket.<ticket>` as the
WebSocket subprotocols of `GET /api/v1/events/ws`. Good once.

device_signature.description: ES256 over the canonical request string, with Ainkrad-Device, Ainkrad-Session, Ainkrad-Alg, Ainkrad-Timestamp and Ainkrad-Nonce alongside (handshake spec §5)
device_signature.name: Ainkrad-Signature

info.description: The Ainkrad Core client API, for the Ainkrad app. Every request is signed by the device's own P-256 key (ES256, raw r||s): the headers Ainkrad-Device, Ainkrad-Session, Ainkrad-Alg (ES256), Ainkrad-Timestamp, Ainkrad-Nonce and Ainkrad-Signature cover an exact canonical string of the Core identity fingerprint, the method, path, query, time, nonce and the body's SHA-256 (handshake spec §5). A session comes from POST /handshake/challenge then POST /handshake/session and lasts 15 minutes; there is no bearer secret, and an Authorization header is refused. A signed body is at most 1 MiB: a larger one is answered 401 auth_failed and counted as a failure against the address, so keep uploads below it. Before trusting a Core, POST /handshake with a fresh nonce and check that core_sig verifies under core_spki and that its fingerprint is the pinned one. Requests carry the server's own Host and no Origin, or the Core's own origin from its web client. A web client signs in with a passkey (POST /handshake/passkey/options, then POST /handshake/passkey/session) and signs every request with a non-extractable WebCrypto P-256 session key in the same way; its event socket takes a one-time ticket (POST /api/v1/ws-ticket) in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol. Times are RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds. Versioning: within /api/v1, enum values, union variants, optional fields and operations may be added; a client must keep an unknown enum value (every enum is open) and skip an event or union variant it cannot decode. Anything removed or renamed is a new /api/v2. `info.version` is `1.<minor>.0`; the minor (`GET /api/v1/me`, `versions.api.minor`) is bumped on every addition.

101.description: Switching to a WebSocket. Each text frame is one `Event` (schema `Event`). Closed with 1013 when the client falls behind (a send blocked too long), with the reason `too slow; resume from the last seq read, at most <seq>`: `<seq>` is the last event the server tried to send. The hint is best effort; the client reconnects with `Last-Event-ID` set to the last seq it actually read. Also closed with 1001 (no pong), 1011 (server error), 4001 (the device was revoked) and 4003 (its scopes changed: reconnect), with the same hint; with 4410 and `past retention, floor <seq>` when the resume point is below the retention floor (re-sync from `/api/v1/events/latest`)

The calling device now gets pushes: what the modules' push rules pick

Every setting with its server-wide value
